key_insight: A grid-size-invariant surrogate model predicts rock–fluid interaction and interface reactions accurately across different discretizations, delivering high-fidelity outputs at a fraction of the computational cost.
problem_solved: High-resolution PDE-based rock–fluid interaction models are computationally expensive and impractical for multi-query tasks (uncertainty quantification, optimization, real-time workflows) because results depend strongly on grid resolution.
method: Train a resolution-agnostic surrogate on multi-resolution simulation data so the learned mapping generalizes across grid sizes.
Incorporate interface-aware/physics-consistent representations or losses to preserve reaction and flow behavior at rock–fluid boundaries.
Validate the surrogate across coarse and fine grids and quantify speed/accuracy trade-offs for multi-query applications.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to plug accurate, fast surrogates into UQ, optimization, and real-time decision pipelines without re-running expensive high-resolution PDE solvers. Reduces compute and accelerates exploration of parameter spaces while maintaining interface fidelity.
visual_elements: Comparison chart: computation time vs accuracy for high-fidelity solver vs grid-invariant surrogate (log-scale speedup annotation).
Schematic showing predictions on coarse and fine grids mapped to the same interface output (illustrates grid-size invariance).
Workflow diagram: multi-resolution simulation data -> interface-aware training -> surrogate -> many fast queries (UQ/optimization).
Heatmap/contour examples of concentration/pressure at rock–fluid interface: high-fidelity reference vs surrogate prediction (difference/error map).
paper_title: Surrogate models for Rock-Fluid Interaction: A Grid-Size-Invariant Approach
paper_authors: Nathalie C. Pinheiro, Donghu Guo, Hannah P. Menke, Aniket C. Joshi, Claire E. Heaney
